title: fix(identity): Invite User offers only the roles the caller may grant, read from the role cap's own table
body:
Fixes #23957
Clause-②: yes

## What changes

A `delegated_admin`'s Invite User dialog offered Owner, Admin and Delegated Admin, and the server's invitation role cap refuses all three for that issuer. Now the dialog offers only what the cap admits for the caller. Both read one table in `@objectstack/spec/identity`, so the offer cannot drift from the refusal.

| invitation role | issuers that may grant it (`INVITATION_ROLE_GRANTORS`) | option `visibleWhen` |
|---|---|---|
| `owner` | `owner` | `'org_owner' in current_user.positions` |
| `admin` | `owner`, `admin` | `'org_owner' in current_user.positions \|\| 'org_admin' in current_user.positions` |
| `delegated_admin` | `owner`, `admin` | same as `admin` |
| `member` | any issuer (`INVITATION_ROLE_ANY_ISSUER`) | none, always offered |

- **`packages/spec/src/identity/invitation-role-grant.ts`** (new; constants and pure helpers only): `INVITATION_ROLE_GRANTORS`, `INVITATION_ROLE_ANY_ISSUER`, `invitationRoleGrantors(role)` (a role outside the closed vocabulary takes the `owner`, `admin` row), `invitationRoleGrantPredicate(role)` (it builds the gate the way `membershipReachPredicate` does: one `mapMembershipRole` projection per grade), `INVITATION_ROLE_OPTIONS`, and the types `InvitationRoleGrantors` and `InvitationRoleOption`. It is exported from `identity/index.ts`, and the `api-surface` and `export-origins` artifacts are regenerated with it.
- **`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-role-cap.ts`**: `isPlainMemberInvitation` and the admission decision now read the table. The grade ladder still resolves the issuer's grade and chooses which refusal text names the reason. Refusals and their texts are unchanged (pin below).
- **`sys-user` / `sys-member` / `sys-invitation` `invite_user`**: the `role` param declares `options: [...INVITATION_ROLE_OPTIONS]` instead of inheriting the field's list. Everything else about the param stays field-backed: type, label, `objectOverride`, `required`. Values, English labels and order are unchanged.
- **i18n**: the option labels now resolve under `_actions.invite_user.params.role.options.VALUE`, because objectui's `actionParamOptionLabel` reads that path for every param option. The bundles are regenerated, and the three translated locales reuse the field's existing option translations. No source-hash residue is left (`check:i18n` OK).

The resulting offer: a `delegated_admin` sees **Member** only; an admin sees **Admin, Delegated Admin, Member**; an owner sees **all four**. The card's done-when says an admin should "still see all of them". The cap has always refused `owner` from an admin, so the offer follows the cap instead (see Acceptance notes).

## Hypothesis 1, measured: an existing mechanism carries it, and objectui needs no change

At objectui `f8267df93a` (`.objectui-sha`):

- `packages/fields/src/resolveActionParams.ts`: `resolvedOptions = authoredOptions ?? normaliseOptions(field.options, …)`. Authored options win over inherited ones, and `resolveOptionLabels` returns them unchanged or rebuilds them by spread, so `visibleWhen` survives.
- `packages/core/src/evaluator/optionRules.ts` `resolveVisibleOptions` filters by each option's `visibleWhen` against the record plus `current_user`. The four option widgets reach it through `useCascadingOptions`.
- `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:285` re-labels each option through `actionParamOptionLabel(object, action, param, value, label)`, which spreads the option and keeps `visibleWhen`.

So no new served field is needed, and no objectui half is filed. One correction to the dispatch's premise: at this pin `normaliseOptions` also spreads inherited entries (`fbc23e094`), so an inherited option would keep `visibleWhen` too. The param still declares its own list, because a `visibleWhen` on the FIELD's options would narrow every `sys_member.role` picker, not only the invite dialog.

## Pins

- `plugin-auth/src/invitation-role-grant-offer.test.ts`
  - **The offer is the door**: for each of the three mirrors and each issuer grade, it evaluates the declared options' `visibleWhen` with `celEngine` against `current_user.positions = [mapMembershipRole(grade)]`, and asserts the offered set equals `{ role : invitationRoleCapFailure(role, grade) === null }`. It also pins delegated_admin → `['member']`, admin → three roles, owner → all four.
  - **The cap is unchanged**: a frozen copy of the pre-table cap is the oracle across a 41 × 37 grid of requested and issuer values: every single role, every two-role comma pair over five names (`sales_manager` included), arrays, case and space variants, and empty or non-string values. Every case gives the same answer with the same text. The test also asserts the grid holds both refusals (more than 100) and admissions.
- `spec/src/identity/invitation-role-grant.test.ts`: the table covers the vocabulary, the unlisted-role row, the predicate text, and that the options keep the vocabulary's values, labels and order.

**Ablation** (one-shot; no permanent file): `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` dropped the `owner` option's `visibleWhen` (anchor 1 → 0, blob `fe0aa9a9` → `8fcec5e6`). After a spec rebuild, `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in `dist/identity/index.{js,mjs}`, and `invitation-role-grant-offer.test.ts` went **red: 10 failed** (every non-owner issuer on all three mirrors, plus the explicit case). The restore was verified: blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, porcelain clean. After a rebuild the marker was absent from all 232 built files, and the test was green again with 14 passed. A static list with no `options` on the param fails the same file's `invite_user declares its own role options` assertion.

## Verification (local, head `4ce40d55`, after merging `origin/main`)

- `@objectstack/plugin-auth` test: 151 files, 2956 passed, 10 skipped. typecheck exit 0.
- `@objectstack/spec` test: 691 files, 20939 passed. typecheck exit 0. `check:generated`: all 14 artifacts up to date.
- `@objectstack/platform-objects` test: 73 files, 1136 passed. typecheck exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs`: OK, 10 packages in sync.
- `dispatch-gates --commands` derived 90 families on `4ce40d55`: 89 exit 0 (`check:role-word` among them, since this diff names roles). `--ran` reconciliation: 90 accounted, 89 run, 1 NOT MEASURED, 0 unrun.
- `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: its fixture needs an unshallowed clone). NOT MEASURED locally; CI reads it.

## Acceptance notes

- **The admin's offer excludes Owner.** The card's done-when reads "an owner or admin still sees all of them". The cap refuses `owner` from an admin, both before and after this PR, so the offer follows the cap. The admin dialog therefore no longer shows Owner. Offering it would keep exactly the offer-then-refuse defect this card closes.
- **A role outside the closed vocabulary** (ADR-0108): the dialog never offers one, because the option list is the closed vocabulary and is not widened. The cap grades it with `invitationRoleGrantors`' administrative row, as before.
- **`resend_invitation`** on `sys_invitation` keeps its field-backed `role` param with `defaultFromRow`. It re-sends the row's own role and is not one of the three `invite_user` mirrors, so it is untouched.
- **Stale docblock, observation only**: `ui/action.zod.ts` (the ActionParam `options` docblock and its `guidance` comment) says objectui's `normaliseOptions` rebuilds inherited entries as `{ label, value }`. At the current pin it spreads them (`fbc23e094`). That is a documentation drift with no runtime effect. Carrier: none.
- The option gate is UI courtesy; the server cap stays the authority. Nothing changes about who the server lets invite whom.
- #23945 (the refusal's missing `code`) is not addressed here.
